outlook.statement: The hotel's performance was adversely impacted during May-June 2025 due to the Indo-Pakistan war, resulting in a slight decrease in total revenue for FY 2025-2026.

Competing hotels and resorts are almost entirely with brand affiliation, carrying benefits of chain marketing, loyalty programs and chain assistance. There is additional competitive question of demand shift in north Goa, particularly after the opening of Mopa airport.

During the Financial Year 2025-26, macroeconomic damage coupled with geopolitical uncertainty, annual occupancy fell by 10.5% (i.e. from 82.0% to 73.4%). Despite this impact on occupancy, the Company was able to report growth in Average Total Revenue Per Occupied Room Per Night (TRevPOR) (after subtracting taxes) by 6.9% from ₹19,725 per room per night in Financial Year 2024-25 to ₹21,086 in the Financial Year 2025-26.

The hospitality industry is expected to grow as there is a supply-demand imbalance. Foreign tourist arrivals are likely to increase, especially if GST rates on hotels are reduced. The wedding segment is achieving a larger share of profits partly due to the 'WED IN INDIA' initiative. The Company has initiated the process of building a larger banquet hall. Road network within Goa has improved and reduced travel time from both Dabolim and Mopa airports. Expansion of Dabolim Airport terminal is nearing completion. Ro-Ro trains from Mumbai to Goa will commence in December. Various world events, such as the 'Chess Championship', are scheduled to be hosted in Goa.

Geopolitical tensions can disrupt travel flows and negatively impact traveller sentiment. Flight disruptions can adversely affect tourist arrivals and overall travel sentiment. Seasonality and adverse weather conditions can lead to fluctuations in tourism demand. Labour shortages and skill gaps could constrain the future growth of the tourism sector.
